_comment: Checks the frame: group sizes are chosen by the investigator, so a case-control study cannot give a rate of disease.

stem.en: A case-control study of a rare tumour enrols 20 patients and 60 people without the tumour. Which statement about these group sizes is correct?

text.en: About a quarter of the people in the source population have the tumour
The tumour must be three times as common as the cases alone suggest
The investigator chose the sizes, and they do not measure how common the tumour is
The controls must outnumber the cases for the comparison to be valid

explanation.en: The number of controls per case is a design choice: one per case when cases are plentiful, and two to four when cases are few. Dividing 20 by the 80 studied adds two groups that the investigator selected, so the result is not a measure of how often the tumour occurs in the population.

hints.en: Ask who decided that there would be 20 cases and 60 controls.
